name: Prince Alwaleed bin Talal
detail: First Saudi signatory to The Giving Pledge (2016), pledging his fortune to philanthropy; private charitable giving, not statutory wealth taxation.

name: G20 Ministerial Declaration Signatories (Rio, 2024)
detail: Saudi delegation agreed to general G20 Rio tax cooperation language on effective taxation of ultra-high-net-worth individuals, without endorsing a net wealth tax.

name: Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud
detail: Crown Prince and Prime Minister who explicitly ruled out introducing personal income taxation or wealth taxation in his televised 2021 Vision 2030 interview.

name: White Land Tax (رسوم الأراضي البيضاء)
detail: Annual 2.5% fee on vacant urban land plots to encourage housing development; a land/property tax excluded under Section 2.

name: Zakat Regulations (ZATCA)
detail: Statutory 2.5% Islamic levy on business capital and working assets of Saudi and GCC nationals and companies; religious jurisprudential duty governed by Sharia principles.

name: Dr. Ihsan Bu-Hulaiga
detail: Prominent Saudi economist who analyzed California billionaire tax and European wealth taxes in Maaal, highlighting valuation and capital mobility challenges without endorsing a wealth tax.

name: Dr. Fahad bin Juma'a
detail: Former Shura Council member and economist who campaigned against the shadow economy, tax and zakat evasion, and advocated electronic payment systems and VAT/excise compliance without calling for a wealth tax.

name: Dr. Said Al-Shaikh
detail: Former chief economist of NCB and former Shura Council Finance Committee member who advocated White Land fees on vacant urban plots to stimulate real estate development; property levy excluded under Section 2.

name: Dr. Hamza Al-Salim
detail: Academic economist who authored comparative studies on Zakat and public taxation and argued in Al-Jazirah for progressive income taxation alongside VAT to pay for public services; income tax excluded under Section 2.

name: Dr. Abdullah Al-Maghlouth
detail: Member of the Saudi Economic Association and real estate economist who focused on implementing the White Land Tax to reduce urban land speculation; excluded land tax under Section 2.

name: Barjas Al-Barjas
detail: Prominent economic analyst who examined VAT, real estate transaction tax, and Zakat contributions to national social welfare, with no proposals for personal wealth taxation.

name: Dr. Nourah Al-Yousef
detail: Chair of the Saudi Economic Association and former Shura Council member who focused on energy economics and sovereign non-oil revenue diversification without advocating a net wealth tax.

name: National Committee of Workers Committees (NCWC)
detail: Saudi national labor representative federation participating in G20 L20 on wages, labor standards, and cost-of-living impacts of VAT, with no proposals for wealth taxation.

name: Essam Al-Zamil
detail: Economic analyst who criticized the expansion of VAT and expat levies on middle-class purchasing power, while supporting White Land fees to fight real estate speculation; no wealth tax advocacy.

name: Dr. Salem Baajajah
detail: Professor of accounting and co-author of standard university textbook on Saudi Zakat and tax collection systems, focusing on technical ZATCA regulations, withholding taxes, and VAT compliance without proposing a net wealth tax.

name: Talat Hafez
detail: Banking expert and former secretary general of the Media and Banking Awareness Committee for Saudi banks who clarified that VAT applies strictly to explicit service fees and not to loans, salaries, or cash withdrawals.

name: Frank Kane
detail: Senior business columnist at Arab News who moderated the 2017 KAEC Top CEO panel where Janahi proposed a 1% wealth tax and reported on it, but did not personally sponsor or endorse a wealth tax proposal.

name: Khalid Abu-Ismail & Vladimir Hlasny
detail: Economists at UN ESCWA in Beirut who authored the 2020 regional technical paper 'Wealth Inequality and Closing the Poverty Gap in Arab Countries: The Case for a Solidarity Wealth Tax', modeling regional redistribution across 14 Arab countries without domestic Saudi policy advocacy; cataloged in global resources.

name: Mohammed Al-Jadaan
detail: Saudi Minister of Finance who repeatedly reaffirmed at G20 and WEF Davos that Saudi Arabia has no plans to introduce personal income or wealth taxation, relying on VAT, corporate taxes on foreign entities, and Zakat.

name: Abdulhamid Al-Amri
detail: Prominent Saudi real estate economist and columnist who advocated aggressively for expanding and escalating the White Land Tax on vacant urban plots to curb real estate speculation; property levy excluded under Section 2.

name: Dr. Raja Almarzoqi
detail: Saudi macroeconomist, GCC General Coordinator for Negotiations, and co-author of Islamic Macroeconomics who analyzes Sharia-compliant public finance and non-oil revenue diversification without endorsing secular wealth taxes.

name: National Assembly Party (NAAS)
detail: Exiled Saudi opposition party founded in 2020; its foundational political manifesto criticizes the imposition of VAT and administrative fees on citizens without democratic accountability, with no wealth tax proposals.

name: Saleh Kamel
detail: Jeddah businessman (died 2020) who said in a CNN Arabic interview of December 2016 that taxes in the Gulf were late, that everyone pays taxes, and that zakat is a kind of tax which in economic terms makes other taxes unnecessary. No wealth tax is named. Page read at Al-Ahram Gate.
